phases: scoped (tier 2): the Worker's scheduler, from the cron to /jobs/tick and back, with the API's wakes (spec §16, D99, D141); db4e5b9..8579176
headline: Both fixes in the area hold. Finding 2's own breakage check is now killed. Both halves of note 11 (a wake, and a later cron, arriving during a tick) are tested and killed. Measured against the real Worker: six crons with nothing due made one tick, and the flow's four crons made one tick, at the job's minute. Two new edits survive the tests, but the behaviour behind both is right today, so neither blocks: forgetting a refused tick, and the later of two wakes during one tick winning.

findings.title: The Worker's only-when-due gate (D141) had no test.
findings.detail: `scheduler.test.ts` now drives `Scheduler.cron()` with stand-in storage. The run-3 check `r3-scheduler-ticks-every-minute` is killed. Measured against the real Worker (`wrangler dev`, the local API on `sen_qa`), counting `jobs_next_once()` calls, which each tick makes once: six crons in 15 s with nothing due made one tick. In FLOW-R3S-1, four crons (one before the test job's minute, two at once after it, one more) made one tick, at the job's minute.
findings.repro: node scripts/mutants.mjs --only r3-scheduler-ticks-every-minute; ticks = pg_stat_user_functions.calls for jobs_next_once (track_functions = 'pl' on sen_qa)

findings.title: `Scheduler.cron()` wrote back the state it had read before a tick.
findings.detail: After the tick, `cron()` now reads the latest state again. It keeps the later `lastCron`, and applies the soonest wake that came during the tick. Both halves are guarded: dropping the merge or the wake fails *wakes sooner when the API asks, and keeps a wake that comes while a tick runs*.

findings.title: No test notices if the scheduler forgets ticks the API refused, which would keep the Worker's /health green while every tick fails.
findings.detail: In `tick()`, if a non-2xx answer returned `afterTick(s, now, undefined)` instead of `afterFailure(s, now)`, every suite would stay green. The retry would still come in 5 minutes, so the new test (*after a failed tick, tries again in five minutes*), which counts only calls, still passes. But `failingSince` would never be set, so the Worker's `/health` would never say `tick`. D141 names *ticks fail for 15 minutes* as one of the monitor's two signals, as when a secret is rotated on one side only. `clock.test.ts` tests `afterFailure()` itself, not that `tick()` calls it. The behaviour is right today, measured end to end: a Worker given the wrong scheduler secret was refused (`tick: 401`, 3 times about 5 minutes apart). Its `/health` stayed `{"ok":true}` until 15:27, then answered 503 `late: [tick]` at 15:29, 16 minutes after the first refusal. Minor rather than Major: `/health/jobs` still fails after 26 hours. A test would hold it by asserting `/health` after a failed tick and 15 minutes.

findings.title: No test holds that, of two wakes during one tick, the sooner one wins.
findings.detail: `wake()` keeps `Math.min(this.woke ?? at, at)` while a tick runs. Replacing it with `at` (the last wake wins) survives, because the test makes only one wake during its tick. With two one-off jobs scheduled during one tick, the later-scheduled one would set the wake, and a sooner job would wait for it. Ticks take seconds, so it's rare.
